proposals.citation: dedr[entry 2248];varghese2015palakkad[Appendix B3, item 87, Mala Malasa, Ancham colony]
proposals.evidence: DEDR2248 gives Tamil/Malayalam kōḻi fowl, Kota kōy, Kodagu kōḷi, Kannada kōḻi and Tulu kōri/kōḷi. These southern survey kōyi/koyɨ/kōḷi/kośi/kojī-type responses are comparative lect extensions, retaining the glide, lateral and palatal/sibilant variants. The source chicken sense is compatible with fowl; this does not merge them with the distinct central-Dravidian kor family. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.citation: dedr[entry 4798];varghese2015palakkad[Appendix B3, item 89, Mala Malasa, Ancham colony]
proposals.evidence: DEDR4798 gives Tamil/Malayalam māṭu ox and Kota māṛ beast, explicitly including cattle and buffalo. The southern survey maḍɨ/maḍu cow responses are comparative lect extensions of this cattle term, with a more specific female-bovine elicitation gloss than the Tamil/Malayalam ox gloss. Preserve that semantic difference and all original vowel-length/voicing notation. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.citation: dedr[entry 4635];varghese2015palakkad[Appendix B3, item 76, Mala Malasa, Ancham colony]
proposals.evidence: DEDR4635 gives Tamil mañcaḷ, Malayalam maññaḷ/mañña, Kannada mañjaḷa, Kodagu mañja and Tulu mañjaḷu turmeric or turmeric-yellow. The selected simple southern survey mañja/mañjal-type turmeric responses are comparative lect extensions preserving palatal nasal/stop spelling, final-lateral loss and vowel notation; no longer compound is reduced to this stem. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4616 explicitly gives Tamil makaṉ and Malayalam makan/mōn son, Kannada maga/makan, Tulu mage and Toda mox child/son. The selected southern survey makan/magan/maga/mahan-type responses preserve the family, including k/g/h variation and nasalized or nasal-cluster lect forms. These minority-lect assignments are comparative proposals; ambiguous contractions and longer compounds are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
